If anyone else runs into the same issue after following suggestions above: 

`brew install binutils` may give the following warning (or something similar) which is easily missed:

```bash
==> Caveats
binutils is keg-only, which means it was not symlinked into /opt/homebrew,
because it shadows the host toolchain.

If you need to have binutils first in your PATH, run:
  echo 'export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/binutils/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc

For compilers to find binutils you may need to set:
  export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/binutils/lib"
  export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/binutils/include"
```

The issue was solved for me by running 

`echo 'export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/binutils/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc`

and setting in CMake:

`
OBJCOPY_PATH:FILEPATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/binutils/bin/objcopy
`

However `>` returns a false _**255.255.254.0**_. In fact I got _**255.255.255.255**_ from this crate method, guess might be cascading errors, haven't checked thoroughly.
Anyway, by changing `>` into `>=` , I am getting the **CORRECT** `netmask` and `broadcast` now, on **Windows**.
Before, I am getting the **CORRECT** `prefix_length` but **WRONG** `netmask` and `broadcast`.

v11.24.0

Features

After Batch 1 (11.19.0) and Batch 2 (11.22.0), this release completes the addition of new parameters to reduce the need for theme-specific ("delta") CSS, with the final Batch 3 of new parameters:

  • Border-width of message strips (sapMessage_BorderWidth) and background-color of hovered buttons in message strips (sapMessage_Button_Hover_Background)
  • A whole new namespace sapTab, that describes tabs in e.g. an IconTabBar with standard text-, foreground-, icon- and background-color, selected state and positive/critical/negative semantic states, e.g. sapTab_Negative_Selected_IconColor
  • Text and background colors for the "b" versions of indication colors, e.g. sapIndicationColor_1b_TextColor

issue.title: ``deno doc --html`` generating incorrect url reference in subpages
issue.body:
This issue seems to correlate with this issue on deno: https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/25069

Link references hon ``deno doc --html`` aren't correctly generated in subpages search queries, missing the last root on the url

I have a production scenario where it doesn't work:

Actually hosting my doc through github pages (*note that even simply opening index.html will result on same issue*): https://rpdjf.github.io/Jikan.js/

Research on the man page works as expected, the links aren't broken:
https://rpdjf.github.io/Jikan.js/?q=jikanclient

But once we are on a subpage, like this:
https://rpdjf.github.io/Jikan.js/~/JikanClient.html

The research query will only display broken url references:
https://rpdjf.github.io/Jikan.js/~/JikanClient.html?q=animeManager

Now, when clicking on any of the search result, we end up with a 404 error, for example:
https://rpdjf.github.io/~/animeManager.html

These new research queries seems to remove the last root of the url, returning:
``https://rpdjf.github.io/~/animeManager.html`` instead of ``https://rpdjf.github.io/Jikan.js/~/animeManager.html``

Using ``deno 2.1.4``

Doc built with ``deno doc --html --name="Jikan.ts" .\src\v4\index.ts`` from root project folder

## About the PR
Changed some drink names to be more SS14 lore themed.

## Why / Balance
There were a lot of differing views regarding a recent suggested change to a drink name in the game, which seemed in danger of descending into debates about real-world politics. I thought that one of the better suggestions to come out of this was to name some drinks with in-game themes. It was also suggested, that in future, it would make more sense to edit the localisation files rather than rename entity IDs, allowing for easier forking and less potential merge conflicts.

This a draft for now, as current changes will cause conflict with an approved PR, and I thought people would want to have some input and be able have their suggestions added to this before it is put up for review.

comment.body:
> is this bait?

Not at all, none of this _needs_ to be changed. If the general sentiment is that this just looks like bait, then I am all for leaving it alone. I was only highlighting those in the context of introducing more lore friendly drink names, without actually adding more individual drinks to the game at this point.

The reason they haven't been touched yet, is precisely because someone might be upset at 'manhattan erasure' or whatever. Something like renaming a cocktial to "The Revolutionary" seemed pretty innocuous, while adding a little atmosphere to the game.

The PR explanations have tried to emphasise that simply erasing real-world references wasn't the driving motivation. It's just circumstantial that a tangential goal for this PR, could include having some more in-universe drink names, over, an arguably, somewhat arbitrary selection of real-world cocktail names.

It also seemed preferable that any major additions, recipe changes, or removals of drinks from the game files was best left to a separate PR; the only proposed initial changes this PR makes, are directly related to comments about an already discussed name change, and a suggested further change that might be a preferable compromise, based on feedback.

# Code Review: Patch to src/Rtsp/RtpReceiver.h

## Summary

This patch modifies the `PacketSortor` class to improve its handling of RTP packet sequencing, particularly in scenarios with sequence number rollovers or out-of-order packets.  The core change replaces the `_last_seq_out` member with `_next_seq`, simplifying the logic and potentially improving efficiency. This is a patch review.

## Detailed Feedback

### Code Overview

The patch refactors the `PacketSortor` class, primarily focusing on how it tracks the next expected sequence number and handles out-of-order packets. The key change is replacing the `_last_seq_out` variable with `_next_seq`, which directly represents the next expected sequence number. This simplifies several calculations and makes the code easier to understand.

### Strengths

- **Improved Readability:** The use of `_next_seq` instead of `_last_seq_out` significantly improves the readability and understandability of the code. The logic is now more straightforward and less prone to errors.
- **Potential Performance Improvement:** By simplifying the calculations, the patch might lead to a slight performance improvement, especially when dealing with a large number of out-of-order packets.
- **Reduced Code Duplication:** The changes reduce some code duplication by centralizing the calculation of the next expected sequence number.

### Areas for Improvement

#### 1.  Error Handling and Logging

- **Issue:** While the code logs dropped packets, it could provide more context.  The log message only indicates the range of dropped packets.  Adding information like the RTP timestamp or packet type would be beneficial for debugging.
- **Suggestion:** Enhance the log message to include more details about the dropped packets, such as RTP timestamp, payload type, and potentially the reason for dropping (e.g., sequence number too far out of order).
- **Example:**

```c++
WarnL << "packet dropped: " << _next_seq << " -> " << static_cast<SEQ>(seq - 1)
      << ", latest seq: " << _latest_seq
      << ", jitter buffer size: " << _pkt_sort_cache_map.size()
      << ", jitter buffer ms: " << _ticker.elapsedTime()
      << ", RTP timestamp: " << packet->getTimestamp()  // Add RTP timestamp
      << ", Payload Type: " << packet->getPayloadType(); // Add payload type
```

#### 2.  Clarity of Comments

- **Issue:** Some comments are automatically translated and might not be entirely accurate or clear in the context of the code.
- **Suggestion:** Review and refine the comments to ensure they accurately reflect the code's functionality and are written in clear, concise English.  Consider removing the "[AUTO-TRANSLATED]" tags once the comments are reviewed.

#### 3.  Testing

- **Issue:**  The patch needs thorough testing to ensure it correctly handles various scenarios, including sequence number rollovers, large numbers of out-of-order packets, and edge cases.
- **Suggestion:**  Add comprehensive unit tests to cover different scenarios and edge cases to verify the correctness and robustness of the changes.


## Conclusion

The patch is a positive improvement to the `PacketSortor` class. The simplification of the sequence number tracking logic enhances readability and potentially performance. However, improvements to logging and the addition of thorough testing are crucial before merging this patch.  Addressing the suggested improvements will make the code more robust, maintainable, and easier to debug.

issue.body:
[kernel log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18266859/kernel.log.txt)
### Describe the bug
After power on and device start up built-in MMC card reader slot does not function, and (even) without SD card inserted error below is reported repeatedly.

[    7.509414] mtk-msdc 10130000.mmc: no support for card's volts
[    7.521080] mmc0: error -22 whilst initialising SDIO card
[    7.532469] init: - preinit -

[    9.010318] mtk-msdc 10130000.mmc: no support for card's volts
[    9.021991] mmc0: error -22 whilst initialising SDIO card
[   10.199853] mmc0: Card stuck being busy! __mmc_poll_for_busy
[   10.244659] mtk-msdc 10130000.mmc: no support for card's volts


### OpenWrt version

r28211-d55754ce0d

### OpenWrt release

24.10.0-rc4

### OpenWrt target/subtarget

ramips/mt76x8

### Device

RAVPower RP-WD009

### Image kind

Official downloaded image

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install 24.10.0-rc4 on RAVPower RP-WD009
2. Observe MMC errors in kernel and system logs.

### Actual behaviour

Builtin MMC card reader does not function, and repeatedly logs error -22.
It does not make a difference if I insert an SD card in the slot or not.

### Expected behaviour

Builtin MMC card reader does function, and logs no errors

### Additional info

I was hoping that the 24.x release/kernel would fix the issue with certain SD cards in the builtin MMC module that I reported with the 23.x release (see [ticket 14042](https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/issues/14042)), and which forced me to stick to the 22.x release. However with rc4 of the new 24.x release, the MMC module does not function at all. It was suggested in the past that [pull request 15896](https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/15896) might solve the issue, but I'm not sure whether that has been followed up on for the 24.x release.

_No response_

- [X] I am reporting an issue for OpenWrt, not an unsupported fork.
